title: Tenant-Aware Edge Quantization and Localization Reference Architecture
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document describes a reference architecture for running model inference in private VPC and on-prem edge locations with tenant-aware quantization and localized model placement. The goal is to reduce per-token cost and network egress while preserving tenant isolation, auditability, and graceful rollback behavior during upgrades. This architecture is targeted at customers using Redwood Private in distributed site configurations (regional edge, branch offices, or regulated data centers).

Key goals
- Lower inference unit cost at the edge via localized quantized model variants.
- Ensure tenant-level security and data separation for multi-tenant private deployments.
- Provide deterministic upgrade and rollback procedures for quantized model artifacts.
- Maintain observability and quality guardrails so regressions are detected and rolled back automatically.

Audience
- Private deployments architects, operators, field engineers, and SREs responsible for edge and VPC customer installs.

High-level architecture

1) Control plane (centralized, Redwood-managed or delegated)
- Model catalog service: authoritative list of model versions and approved quantized variants.
- Rollout controller: governs multi-site model rollouts, canaries, and staged rollbacks.
- Policy engine: tenant policies, regulatory constraints, allowed quantization levels, and evidence collection rules.

2) Data plane (deployed at customer VPC / on-prem edge sites)
- Local runtime nodes (GPU/accelerator hosts) running Redwood inference runtime.
- Local model store: signed artifact repository for compressed / quantized weights.
- Tenant isolation layer: network and filesystem sandbox per tenant (namespaces, service accounts, iptable segments).
- Telemetry & evidence sink: encrypted telemetry forwarding to an operator-defined telemetry gateway or S3-compatible bucket for audits.

3) Optional satellite cache tier
- A regional cache for larger model families to avoid repeated downloads for nearby sites (useful for clusters of branch offices).

Diagram (textual)
Control Plane (Redwood) --> Secure Channel --> Site Gateway --> Local Runtime (per-tenant namespaces) --> Local Model Store (signed artifacts)
                                                                         
Key concepts and terminology
- Quantized variant: a model artifact produced with a specific quantization profile (e.g., int8-q4, fp16, trimmed-embed). Each variant is cryptographically signed and has a quality metadata bundle (eval metrics, validation prompts).
- Tenant policy: per-tenant constraints declared in the control plane (allowed quantization levels, telemetry consent, egress allowances).
- Localization: selecting a model variant to deploy at site based on tenant policy, site capacity, latency SLOs, and auditability requirements.

Preflight checklist (operator)
1. Network and KMS
   - Verify site-to-control-plane TLS tunnel exists and uses mutual TLS.
   - Confirm KMS/HSM integration for local key wrapping (key IDs present and test decrypt succeeds).
2. Hardware
   - Validate accelerator drivers (NVIDIA driver >= 525, or equivalent) and CUDA/cuDNN versions per runtime matrix.
   - Confirm available GPU memory and local storage to hold compressed artifacts (table below).
3. Policy and governance
   - Ensure tenant policies are loaded in control plane and reachable by site.
   - Check evidence collection endpoint and retention policy match customer contract.
4. Smoke verification
   - Run synthetic workload against a canary quantized variant and compare quality metrics to baseline.

Model artifact sizing guidance (example table)
| Model family | Baseline size (FP16) | Typical int8-q4 size | Expected local disk per-tenant (2 variants) |
|--------------|----------------------|----------------------:|---------------------------------------------:|
| Llama-2-13B  | 26 GB                | 13 GB                | 28 GB                                        |
| Mosaic-7B    | 14 GB                | 7 GB                 | 15 GB                                        |
| Tiny-Embed   | 0.8 GB               | 0.4 GB               | 1.0 GB                                       |

Decision matrix for localization (summary)
- If tenant latency SLO < 50ms and site GPU available: deploy heavy fp16 or int8-q4 locally.
- If tenant data residency forbids model egress: prefer locally stored variants regardless of size.
- If site has limited storage (<100GB) and serves many tenants: use satellite cache + thin runtime (streaming from cache with local KV).

Deployment and rollout procedure (canary-first, staged)
1. Authorize and sign quantized variant in model catalog.
2. Create rollout plan in control plane: define canary site(s), percent traffic, and rollback thresholds (quality and latency).
3. Push artifact metadata to site; site downloads artifact over secure channel into a staging path (/var/lib/redwood/staging).
4. Site runs local verification suite (synthetic prompts + perf microbench).
5. If local checks pass, promote artifact to active path and update local routing to point tenant traffic at the new variant.
6. Control plane monitors evaluation signals for the configured window (default 4 hours). If thresholds are exceeded, automatic rollback triggers: local runtime switches back to previous variant and control plane creates a rollback ticket.

Rollback considerations and forensic evidence
- All model promotions and rollbacks must record:
  - artifact id and checksum
  - promoter identity (user/service) and timestamp
  - validation suite outputs (evaluation prompt set score delta)
  - telemetry snapshot (latency histogram, error rate) for the last 30 minutes
- Evidence retention: by default keep a compressed evidence bundle for 90 days; regulated customers may require longer (set via tenant policy).

Operational runbook (day-2 ops)
- Monitoring and Alerts
  - SLO breach alert: latency P99 > tenant SLO for 10 minutes -> page oncall and trigger probe job.
  - Quality regression alert: moving-average quality score drops >3% vs baseline -> create investigation ticket and pause further rollouts.
  - Artifact integrity alert: artifact checksum mismatch on download -> quarantine artifact and notify vendor.
- Common remediation steps
  1. If latency regresses after quantized promotion: scale up local runtime pool or switch to higher-capacity variant (fp16).
  2. If quality regresses: perform immediate rollback, preserve evidence bundle, and rerun local validation suite against baseline.
  3. If disk pressure: remove non-active variants older than 30 days or trigger eviction to satellite cache.

Security and compliance notes
- Cryptographic signing: require every quantized variant to be signed by Redwood or customer-managed signing key. Verify signatures during local promotion.
- Telemetry filtering: tenant policy can redact or exclude prompt text from telemetry. Only publish hashed prompt identifiers to central telemetry by default.
- Audit logs: include operator actions, promotion and rollback events, and KMS key usage logs in a tamper-evident bundle.

Configuration reference (example values)
- rollout.window: 4h
- rollout.canary_percent: 5
- validation.prompt_set_id: tenant-default-v1
- acceptable_quality_delta: -2.5%
- local.storage.active_variant_limit: 3
- evidence.retention_days: 90

Testing and validation suite (recommended)
- Unit: artifact signature verification, checksum, and unpack tests.
- Integration: runtime end-to-end inference on a held-out prompt set (compare to baseline).
- Stress: high-QPS synthetic traffic to validate batching and latency under load.
- Chaos: simulate transient disk failures and control-plane disconnects to validate safe rollback/evacuation.

Recommended ownership and escalation matrix
- Model catalog & rollout controller: Product / Applied ML (primary), Eng Platform (secondary).
- Site runtime & day-2 ops: Customer Success / Field Engineering (primary), Eng SRE (secondary).
- Security & keys: Security Team (primary).

Appendix: Example CLI snippets
- Fetch artifact metadata from control plane (pseudo-CLI):
  redwoodctl artifact get --id artifact-1234 --site eu-berlin

- Promote staged artifact locally:
  sudo redwood-runtime promote --staging /var/lib/redwood/staging/artifact-1234 --tenant tenant-acme

- Rollback to previous variant:
  sudo redwood-runtime rollback --tenant tenant-acme --to previous

Related documents
- See the telemetry ingestion and retention guide for evidence packaging rules.
- See the operator handoff and field runtime handbook for cutover responsibilities.

Open questions and future work
- Automated per-tenant quantization tuning: can we safely autotune quantization level per workload without manual baseline evaluation?
- Disk tiering policy: evaluate a hot/warm/cold split for variants to further reduce footprint.
